Your own project

Source: vignettes/Your-Own-Project.Rmd
Your-Own-Project.Rmd

A project starts with a mapping file that lists your samples, and one command that sets up the project folder. After that, everything happens in the app, the same way as in Get started.

The mapping file

The mapping file is a CSV file with one row per sample. For example:

ID,Taxon,R1,R2,Voucher
Fish_01,Brosme brosme,Fish_01_R1.fastq.gz,Fish_01_R2.fastq.gz,USNM 123456
Fish_02,Upeneus parvus,SRR22396758/SRR22396758_1.fastq.gz,SRR22396758/SRR22396758_2.fastq.gz,USNM 123457
Snail_01,Tritia reticulata,Snail_01_R1.fq.gz,Snail_01_R2.fq.gz,

The rules:

  • Columns. It needs the columns ID, Taxon, R1, and R2. Upper and lower case do not matter in column names.
  • Taxon. Give the species name whenever you can (for example Upeneus parvus), spelled as NCBI has it; a genus or higher group works when the species is unknown. RiboPilot uses it to pick the reference database and the quality checks, to judge contamination, and as the organism name in your GenBank records.
  • IDs. Each ID must be unique, ignoring case, and at most 40 characters long. Use only letters, digits, dash (-), underscore (_), and colon (:): no spaces, dots, or slashes.
  • Commas only. Save the file with commas between values. From Excel, use File > Save As > CSV UTF-8 (Comma delimited).
  • Paired reads only. Every sample with Illumina reads needs both an R1 and an R2 file. Single-end reads are not currently supported.
  • Read file names are relative to the read folder you pass as data_path. Subfolders are fine (SRR22396758/SRR22396758_1.fastq.gz), but full paths are not.
  • No spaces or special characters in paths. File names, folder names, and the project path may use only letters, digits, and ., _, -, and /. RiboPilot stops and names each path it cannot pass to Docker, Singularity, or Nextflow, for example one with a space or a quote mark.
  • Extra columns are kept, and you can use them in your GenBank headers, for example as {Voucher}. A column name with a space or a dash is read with a dot in its place, so Voucher ID becomes {Voucher.ID}. The Your mapping columns chips in the Export window show every name.
  • Metadata ID columns. Columns named GEOME_BCID, GBIF_ID, and BioSample hold a sample’s GEOME, GBIF, and NCBI identifiers. RiboPilot fetches those records when it sets up the project. Blank cells are fine. To use other column names, pass mapping_geome, mapping_gbif, or mapping_ncbi to the new_project() function. See Sample metadata.
  • Reserved names. RiboPilot adds some columns itself, so your file cannot use these names: taxid, sci_name, rank, match_type, tax_alternatives, lineage, lineage_taxids, ref_id, user_group, ref_source, taxonomy_switch, taxonomy_lock, and time_stamp.

The IDs end up in your GenBank records, so choose them with care.

Create the project 

RiboPilot::new_project(
  path       = "~/my_project",
  mapping_fn = "~/my_samples.csv",
  data_path  = "~/my_reads"
)

RiboPilot checks the mapping file and the read files before it writes anything, and stops with an error message if it encounters any issues.

By default, new_project() assumes you are running RiboPilot on a local workstation (i.e. a desktop or laptop). For projects on a computing cluster, pass your cluster profile as executor; see Running on a cluster.

An NCBI API key is optional; see Installation for where to put it.

Once the project is created, open the app and follow the five steps, as in Get started.

RiboPilot::RiboPilot("~/my_project")

Run a handful of samples through every step before you run hundreds: settings that are wrong for your group are much cheaper to find on a small run. Make sure to do the Reference step before running the Assemble workflow.

Already have an assembly?

If you have a genome assembly for a sample, or just the contig that contains the ribosomal repeat, you can use it instead of assembling from reads. Add an Assembly column to your mapping file naming that sample’s FASTA file, and pass the folder that holds them as assembly_path:

RiboPilot::new_project(
  path          = "~/my_project",
  mapping_fn    = "~/my_samples.csv",
  data_path     = "~/my_reads",
  assembly_path = "~/my_assemblies"
)

The assembly files must be FASTA files, all gzipped (.gz) or all uncompressed in one project, and named relative to assembly_path.

RiboPilot searches each supplied assembly for rRNA genes and carries forward the contigs that carry an 18S or 28S anchor. A single ribosomal contig passes this search without doing anything special. If you supplied a fragment too short to carry an anchor (an ITS-only sequence, for example), turn the search off in the app’s Assembly Options and RiboPilot uses your file exactly as given.

A sample with an assembly does not need reads: leave R1 and R2 blank in the mapfile. If your file has no reads at all, you can leave out the R1 and R2 columns and data_path entirely. A sample with no reads gets no depth profile, since there is nothing to map back.

Adding samples later

To add samples to a project you have already started, write a mapping file that lists only the new samples, and run:

RiboPilot::add_samples(
  "~/my_project",
  mapping_fn = "~/more_samples.csv",
  data_path  = "~/my_reads"
)

It runs the same checks as new_project(), and refuses IDs that are already in the project. Put the new read files in the same folder as the project’s other reads (the data_path you gave new_project()). The new samples then appear in the Taxonomy step, ready to assign.

To fix or add metadata, such as a voucher number, for samples that are already in the project, list them in a mapping file with the new values and run RiboPilot::update_sample_metadata() the same way. It never changes a sample’s reads, assembly, state, or locks.

Do not rerun new_project() with force = TRUE on a project you have worked on: it deletes all existing results.

What is in the project folder

The project folder holds your results database, its settings, and the pipeline’s working files. The table in Disk space, caches, and offline use says what each item is and when you can safely delete them.
